extracted.intended_audience: WHO Member States, national public health authorities, risk communication practitioners and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, delivering and sustaining risk communication in public health emergencies, and for building local capacity to communicate effectively. Targeted at national authorities and partners responsible for communicating health risks to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk communication as a core IHR function
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is one of the eight core functions that WHO Member States must fulfill as signatories to the International Health Regulations (2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member States are expected to integrate risk communication into their IHR obligations and national preparedness planning; treat risk communication as an essential public health function rather than an optional activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk communication as part of pandemic preparedness (PIP Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is also a component of global and country preparedness for an influenza pandemic, as part of the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure risk communication planning and activities are incorporated into pandemic preparedness frameworks and exercises (e.g., PIP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating during public health emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline is expected to cover communicating during public health emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers principles and practices for messaging, channels, timing, coordination, and actions during acute events; includes rapid response, tailoring to affected populations, and coordination among authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building and sustaining local capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The guideline is expected to cover building and sustaining local capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on long-term systems strengthening: training, institutionalizing risk communication functions, resource planning, workforce development and maintaining readiness between emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance should be comprehensive, evidence-based, up-to-date and systems-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: While principles, good practices and training programmes already exist in the field of risk communication, there is no single, comprehensive, evidence-based, up-to-date, systems-focused WHO guidance for Member States in this area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New guidance should synthesize evidence, incorporate up-to-date lessons from recent emergencies, and adopt a systems perspective (not just isolated techniques) to be useful to Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure communications are credible and based on scientific evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: People are confronted with health advice from multiple sources, and it can be difficult to determine which are credible and based on scientific evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications must emphasize credibility and scientific basis; proactively address misinformation and multiple competing information sources so audiences can identify trustworthy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate rapidly and effectively; address barriers across stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent public health emergencies ... have highlighted enormous challenges in communicating risk to affected populations. They have underscored the barriers faced by national authorities, civil society, and international agencies when they need to communicate rapidly and effectively during such events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for rapid-message development and dissemination; identify and mitigate operational, institutional, cultural and logistical barriers that impede timely and effective communication across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design communication for behavioural impact (COMBI planning steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication for behavioural impact (COMBI) - field workbook: Field workbook for COMBI planning steps in outbreak response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use COMBI planning steps to design interventions aimed at achieving specific behaviour change outcomes during outbreak response; include situation analysis, audience segmentation, and measurable behaviour objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use COMBI toolkit for community outbreak prevention and control
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication for behavioural impact (COMBI) - toolkit: This interagency (FAO, UNICEF, WHO) toolkit will be useful for anyone wanting to design effective outbreak prevention and control measures in community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply COMBI toolkit methods for community-level prevention and control communications; tailor tools to local contexts and involve community stakeholders in planning and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communications training and participant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Communications: Participants handbook (and related materials) provide guidance on effective communication during public health emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participant handbooks and training materials to build skills in message development, media engagement, community engagement and risk communication practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective media communication during public health emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Media Communication during Public Health Emergencies: a WHO field guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow best practices for interacting with media during emergencies: prepare spokespeople, craft clear messages, coordinate messaging across agencies, and anticipate media dynamics to avoid confusion and misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outbreak communication: Best practices for public communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Outbreak communication: Best practices for communicating with the public during an outbreak (report of WHO Expert Consultation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt established best practices for public-facing outbreak communication including transparency, timeliness, audience-centred messaging, and continuous evaluation of communication impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO outbreak communication guidelines (account for outbreak uniqueness)
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO outbreak communication guidelines: 'Disease outbreaks are inevitable, and often unpredictable, events. The environment surrounding an outbreak is unique in all of public health.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply WHO guidelines that recognize the unpredictability and uniqueness of outbreak environments; plan flexible communication strategies that can adapt to changing epidemiology and social contexts.
